comparison: Strong agreement on developmental emergence of feeding rhythms (C5, C6, C15-C19). Both evaluations find evidence convincing with rigorous behavioral assays. OpenEval additionally includes C58 (low sugar paradigm validation) which peer review addresses separately in R2.

Both support dietary manipulation findings (C20-C23, C58) showing low sugar increases feeding and disrupts sleep/LTM. OpenEval additionally includes NPF+ activation effects (C7-C8, C27-C30) which peer review addresses separately in R3.

Both support NPF+ neuron activation findings (C24-C26). Peer review additionally includes LTM/STM effects (C27-C30) which OpenEval addresses in R2. Both note convincing evidence, though OpenEval suggests temperature controls needed.

Significant disagreement on gaboxadol/sleep induction experiments (C31-C40). OpenEval finds claims supported despite developmental defects. Peer review expresses concern that proper L3-like sleep was not induced, questioning the interpretation. OpenEval includes C74 (energetic unsustainability) which peer review addresses in R10.

Both strongly support DN1a-Dh44 calcium imaging findings (C41-C42) showing stage-specific and nutrition-dependent connectivity. Peer review describes this as 'key experimental finding.' OpenEval includes C9, C75-C76, C80 on developmental plasticity; peer review includes these in broader context.

Both support CCHa1 peptide application experiments (C43-C47, C78-C79) demonstrating stage-specific and nutrition-dependent responsiveness. OpenEval focuses on competency development interpretation; peer review integrates this with calcium imaging as part of key circuit findings.

Both support glucose metabolic gene knockdown findings (C48-C53, C57, C83). Peer review notes 'some genetic controls seem inconsistent' due to behavioral variability, while OpenEval finds evidence well-supported. OpenEval includes C10 which peer review addresses in R7.

Both support amino acid sensing gene findings (C54-C56) showing no effect on sleep rhythms. OpenEval notes possible redundant pathway compensation. Peer review includes these claims within broader metabolic gene discussion alongside glucose metabolism findings.

Both support main conclusions (C11, C82) that nutrition influences circuit development and sleep/LTM formation. Peer review describes findings as 'valuable' and 'convincing.' OpenEval notes causal link between energetics and circuit formation is correlative. OpenEval includes C87 (model) which peer review addresses in R10.

Both address speculative claims (C88-C91) about CCHa1-R regulation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct evidence, while peer review implicitly accepts as reasonable interpretation without challenge. Both acknowledge speculative nature.

Both support background claims on L2/L3 transition and prior work (C1-C2, C59-C63, C92). OpenEval emphasizes current study extends prior findings; peer review acknowledges this as established framework the study builds upon.

Partial overlap on developmental context claims (C1-C2, C59-C60). Both accept these as supported background. Peer review R9 covers broader literature context (C12-C14, C64-C72, C85-C86) which OpenEval addresses in separate results.

Both support connection between developmental sleep disruption and memory (C72-C73, C27-C28). OpenEval cites prior literature convergence with current data; peer review accepts as part of established framework from prior lab work.

Both support interpretation of functional differences between larval and adult Dh44 neurons (C84, C70-C71). OpenEval finds interpretation reasonable but suggests direct comparison would strengthen conclusion. Peer review implicitly accepts without challenge.

Both address conservation claims (C85-C86). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting evidence is correlative in mice and lacks mechanistic comparison. Peer review does not challenge these claims, implicitly accepting as reasonable contextual framing.

Both support dissociability of sleep and feeding (C93-C94). OpenEval emphasizes nuanced interpretation showing some manipulations affect both behaviors. Peer review includes C93 within metabolic gene discussion without specific comment on dissociability.

Both support background literature on developmental rhythms in rodents/humans (C12-C14). OpenEval notes these provide study motivation; peer review implicitly accepts as part of broader contextual framework without challenge.

Both support background literature on developmental changes across species (C64-C69). OpenEval suggests authors should verify citations support specific claims; peer review implicitly accepts as appropriate contextual framework.

Both support prior work on DN1a-Dh44 circuit and LTM (C3-C4). OpenEval notes readers should consult original paper for details; peer review explicitly acknowledges this as established prior work from same lab that current study builds upon.
